newsitem.title: USA: Allied Signal profits rise 16 percent.
newsitem.headline: Allied Signal profits rise 16 percent.

text.p: AlliedSignal Inc. reported a 16 percent rise in fourth-quarter profits, and the auto parts and aerospace company's chief executive said it has stepped up its search for acquisitions.
The Morristown, N.J.-based company said its profits rose to $270 million, or 96 cents a share, in the fourth quarter, from $233 million, or 83 cents a share, a year earlier.
AlliedSignal had revenues of $3.5 billion vs. $3.8 billion in the year-ago quarter.
AlliedSignal Chief Executive Lawrence Bossidy said in a telephone interview he expected earnings to grow 13 percent to 17 percent in 1997.

For the year, the company had record profits of $1.02 billion, or $3.61 a share, on revenues of $13.97 billion, a 17 percent increase from 1995 net income of $875 million, or $3.09 a share, on revenues of $14.35 billion.
It was the the fifth year in a row profits had increased 15 percent or more, the company said.

Driving 1996 results were higher sales and double-digit net income increases for airplane engines, equipment systems and electronic systems; auto turbochargers, filters and spark plugs and polymers, fluorines and speciality chemicals, the company said.

The company -- with a war chest of $1.8 billion in cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments after its sale of its auto brake business last year -- has intensified its search for acquisitions, Bossidy said.

AlliedSignal is looking to buy companies or units that complement its speciality chemicals, auto turbocharger and airplane part businesses, he said. He said the company is confident it will complete some purchases.
AlliedSignal noted that its net debt as a percentage of total capital has declined to 9.1 percent from 30.9 percent at the end of 1995.

Bossidy said AlliedSignal will continue its high level of investment in current operations, and expects the company to spend $350 million to $380 million on research and development and about $750 million on capital expenditures.
AlliedSignal stock dropped 12.5 cents to $69.875 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
